## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

14	## 2. 前置知识
15	
16	**什么是数据增强（data augmentation）。** 训练集里的每张图片，经过一次随机几何或颜色扰动（旋转、平移、剪切、变色调……）后，标签不变——一只猫旋转 15 度还是猫。增强相当于告诉模型「这些变化不改变类别」，把不变性先验注入训练。从数学上看，普通训练最小化经验风险
17	
18	\[
19	\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} \ell\!\left(f(x_i), y_i\right),
20	\]
21	
22	而增强训练把每个样本扩展成一个随机变换 \(t\) 下的期望：
23	
24	\[
25	\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathbb{E}_{t\sim\mathcal{T}}\left[\ell\!\left(f(t(x_i)), y_i\right)\right],
26	\]
27	
28	其中 \(\mathcal{T}\) 是增强策略定义的变换分布。有效样本分布被「撑大」了，模型更难死记训练集，从而缓解过拟合。
29	
30	**增强为什么只作用于训练集。** 训练集的目标是「让模型学得会」，注入随机性能提高泛化；验证/测试集的目标是「稳定地度量」，如果评估时每次取样都施加随机旋转，同一模型两次评估的成绩都会抖动，指标就失去了可比性。所以 u4-l3 讲过的双 transform 模式（训练集挂随机增强、验证/测试集只挂确定性变换）在这里再次出现。
31	
32	**新旧两代增强。** 传统做法是手工挑几条规则，比如 `RandomCrop` + `RandomHorizontalFlip`（u3-l2 的 AlexNet notebook 里已经见过类似的随机裁剪思想）。本讲的两件主角是「新式」策略：

154	### 4.2 AutoAugment：搜索出来的增强策略
155	
156	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
157	
158	AutoAugment（Cubuk et al., 2019, [arXiv:1805.09501](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.09501)）把「设计增强规则」本身当成一个搜索问题：在代理任务上用强化学习为每个数据集搜出一套策略，策略由 25 个**子策略（sub-policy）**组成，每个子策略是两个有序操作 \((OP_1, P_1, M_1) \to (OP_2, P_2, M_2)\)，其中 \(P\) 是应用概率、\(M\) 是幅度（如旋转多少度、剪切多大）。训练时：
159	
160	```text
161	取一张图 x
162	    │
163	    ├─ 从 25 个子策略中均匀随机抽 1 个（概率 1/25）
164	    ├─ 以概率 P1 执行操作1（强度 M1），否则跳过
165	    └─ 以概率 P2 执行操作2（强度 M2），否则跳过
166	```
167	
168	CIFAR-10 策略用到的算子包括剪切、平移、旋转、色调/对比度/锐度调整、Posterize、Solarize、AutoContrast、Equalize 等。对普通使用者来说，这些搜索结果已内置在 torchvision 中——`transforms.autoaugment.AutoAugmentPolicy.CIFAR10` 一个枚举值就是整套 25 子策略。
169	
170	它与手工增强（`RandomCrop` + `RandomHorizontalFlip`）的本质区别：手工增强靠人的直觉挑选两三种固定扰动；AutoAugment 靠数据搜出一大张「操作×概率×幅度」的组合表，扰动空间丰富得多。
171	
172	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
173	
174	接入方式只是 u4-l3 Compose 流水线的一次「插拔」：
175	
176	```text
177	transforms.Compose([
178	    transforms.Resize(32),                                  # 确定性：先统一尺寸
179	    transforms.AutoAugment(AutoAugmentPolicy.CIFAR10),      # 随机增强：PIL 域
180	    transforms.ToTensor(),                                  # PIL → Tensor，值域 [0,1]
181	])
182	        │
183	        └─ 注入 Cifar10DataModule(train_transform=...)
184	                │
185	                └─ 其余一切（模型/优化器/Trainer/seed）与基线相同
186	```
187	
188	注意增强操作的位置：**在 `Resize` 之后、`ToTensor` 之前**——AutoAugment 的算子工作在 PIL 图像域，遵守 u4-l3 讲过的固定顺序「PIL 域变换 → ToTensor → （可选 Normalize）」。
189	
190	增强对训练动态的影响：训练损失下降变慢（同一张图每个 epoch 长得都不一样，模型更难死记），因此需要**多得多的 epoch** 才能兑现收益——这正是 notebook 把 `max_epochs` 从 40 提到 500 的原因。

254	### 4.3 TrivialAugmentWide：免调参增强与三组对照
255	
256	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
257	
258	TrivialAugmentWide（Müller & Hutter, 2021, [arXiv:2103.10158](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10158)）是对 AutoAugment 复杂性的反思：既然搜索那么贵，干脆**不搜索**。规则简单到一段话讲完——
259	
260	```text
261	取一张图 x
262	    ├─ 从算子池 {Rotate, ShearX, ShearY, TranslateX, TranslateY, Color, Contrast,
263	    │            Brightness, Sharpness, Posterize, Solarize, AutoContrast, Equalize, Identity}
264	    │            中均匀随机抽 1 个
265	    ├─ 从 [0, num_magnitude_bins] 均匀随机抽一个强度（默认 31 档，"Wide" 即指强度范围宽）
266	    └─ 无条件应用（没有 AutoAugment 那样的应用概率 P）
267	```
268	
269	没有任何在目标任务上搜出来的参数，跨数据集零适配。论文结论是它以近乎零的成本追平或超过搜索类方法——「简单基线的胜利」。
270	
271	对使用者的意义：AutoAugment 需要为数据集挑选对应 policy（`AutoAugmentPolicy.CIFAR10`/`IMAGENET`/`SVHN`），换数据集要动脑；TrivialAugmentWide 换数据集什么都不用改。本讲最后一组对照会检验：在这套仓库配置下，免调参的 TrivialAugment 是否真的不输 AutoAugment。

342	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
343	
344	**练习 1**：`TrivialAugmentWide()` 连 `AutoAugmentPolicy` 这样的参数都没有。这为什么反而是优点？
345	
346	**答案**：AutoAugment 的 policy 是按数据集搜索的，换数据集（甚至换图像统计特性）就要重新选择；TrivialAugmentWide 无任何数据集相关参数，跨任务零配置，避免选错 policy 的风险。对教学与快速实验，「一行接入、无需决策」的价值很大。

352	**练习 3**：假设你要把本讲增强迁移到自己的 10 类工业缺陷检测数据集（每类仅几百张图），先试哪种？要注意什么？

354	**答案**：先试 TrivialAugmentWide（零配置、对中小数据集通常稳健），但要审查算子是否破坏任务语义——例如缺陷颜色本身就是判别特征时，`Color`/`Solarize` 等颜色扰动可能抹掉类别差异；旋转若破坏方向语义（如文字、裂纹走向）也应排除。增强注入的是「标签不变的先验」，先验错了就帮倒忙。

381	   - 早期（前 10 epoch）无增强组 val_acc 领先，增强组因随机扰动收敛慢；

386	## 6. 本讲小结
387	
388	- **数据增强 = 把标签不变的随机扰动注入训练集**，数学上是最小化 \(\mathbb{E}_{t\sim\mathcal{T}}[\ell(f(t(x)),y)]\)，用收敛速度换泛化上限；评估必须保持确定性，故 transform 分「训练随机 / 评估确定」两套，`Cifar10DataModule` 的双参数注入接口正是为此设计。
389	- **AutoAugment** 用搜索得到的 25 子策略（操作×概率×幅度）丰富扰动空间，一行 `transforms.AutoAugment(AutoAugmentPolicy.CIFAR10)` 接入；**TrivialAugmentWide** 零参数、随机算子+宽范围随机强度，免调参却在本对照中效果最好。
390	- 三组对照（同一模型/优化器/seed/划分）：无增强 68.51%（40 epoch）→ AutoAugment 78.30%（500 epoch）→ TrivialAugment 81.68%（1000 epoch）；增强操作插入位置固定在 `Resize` 之后、`ToTensor` 之前（PIL 域）。

# 数据增强实战：AutoAugment 与 TrivialAugment

> 本讲引用 `.ipynb` 文件的行号时，指的是 notebook JSON 文件中的行号（GitHub 上点击链接即可跳转到对应位置）；引用 `.py` 文件时即为普通源码行号。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清楚「数据增强为什么只作用于训练集」，并对照 `Cifar10DataModule` 的双 transform 接口理解它的工程实现。
2. 会用一行 `transforms.AutoAugment(...)` 与 `transforms.TrivialAugmentWide(...)` 把新式增强策略接入训练管线，并知道它们该插在 Compose 流水线的哪个位置。
3. 会组织「受控对照实验」来度量增强收益：固定模型、优化器、随机种子，只改 transform，用验证准确率曲线与测试准确率下结论。
4. 养成批判性读码习惯：本讲的三份 notebook 里就藏着几处复制粘贴遗留与口径偏差，我们逐一指出。

## 2. 前置知识

**什么是数据增强（data augmentation）。** 训练集里的每张图片，经过一次随机几何或颜色扰动（旋转、平移、剪切、变色调……）后，标签不变——一只猫旋转 15 度还是猫。增强相当于告诉模型「这些变化不改变类别」，把不变性先验注入训练。从数学上看，普通训练最小化经验风险

\[
\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} \ell\!\left(f(x_i), y_i\right),
\]

而增强训练把每个样本扩展成一个随机变换 \(t\) 下的期望：

\[
\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathbb{E}_{t\sim\mathcal{T}}\left[\ell\!\left(f(t(x_i)), y_i\right)\right],
\]

其中 \(\mathcal{T}\) 是增强策略定义的变换分布。有效样本分布被「撑大」了，模型更难死记训练集，从而缓解过拟合。

**增强为什么只作用于训练集。** 训练集的目标是「让模型学得会」，注入随机性能提高泛化；验证/测试集的目标是「稳定地度量」，如果评估时每次取样都施加随机旋转，同一模型两次评估的成绩都会抖动，指标就失去了可比性。所以 u4-l3 讲过的双 transform 模式（训练集挂随机增强、验证/测试集只挂确定性变换）在这里再次出现。

**新旧两代增强。** 传统做法是手工挑几条规则，比如 `RandomCrop` + `RandomHorizontalFlip`（u3-l2 的 AlexNet notebook 里已经见过类似的随机裁剪思想）。本讲的两件主角是「新式」策略：

- **AutoAugment**（Cubuk et al., 2019）：用强化学习在目标数据集上**搜索**出 25 个「子策略」，每个子策略含两个图像操作、每个操作带应用概率与幅度；训练时每张图随机抽一个子策略执行。
- **TrivialAugmentWide**（Müller & Hutter, 2021）：反其道而行——**免调参**。每张图随机抽一个算子、随机抽一个强度，直接应用，不搜索任何策略，却在很多任务上追平甚至超过 AutoAugment。

**承接前讲。** 本讲处在 u8 单元：u8-l1 讲过 `LightningModule` / `LightningDataModule` / `Trainer` 三件套，本讲的训练代码全部交给这套机制；u4-l3 讲过 `transforms.Compose` 的固定顺序「几何/颜色变换（PIL 域）→ ToTensor → Normalize」，本讲的增强操作正是插在最前面的 PIL 域。另外请带着 u3-l5 的教训来读：**比较模型必须对齐训练配方**——本讲的对照实验正是这条方法论的正面示范（但也有几处不完美，见 4.3）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

本讲的四份文件位于 `pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/` 目录，构成一个天然的「三胞胎对照实验 + 一份共享工具」：

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| [helper_utilities.py](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/helper_utilities.py) | 三份 notebook 共享的 `LightningModel`、`Cifar10DataModule`（双 transform 接口）与绘图函数 |
| [without-augmentation.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/without-augmentation.ipynb) | 无增强基线：ResNet-18 从零训练 CIFAR-10，40 epoch |
| [with-autoaugment.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/with-autoaugment.ipynb) | 同一模型同一配方，仅给训练集加 AutoAugment（CIFAR10 策略），500 epoch |
| [with-trivialaugment.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/with-trivialaugment.ipynb) | 同上，仅换成 TrivialAugmentWide，1000 epoch |

三份 notebook 开头都注明了互相参照关系（基线 notebook 的第一个 markdown 单元明确写着它是另外两份的 baseline），且都运行在 torch 1.13.1 + lightning 1.9.0 + torchvision 0.14.1 的环境上（`%watermark` 输出）。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 无增强基线与双 transform 数据模块

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

要度量「增强带来多少收益」，先得有一个不含增强的基线。本模块精读两样东西：

1. `Cifar10DataModule`——数据管线如何同时容纳「训练用 transform」与「评估用 transform」两套配置；
2. without-augmentation notebook——基线训练怎么跑起来。

这个 DataModule 与 u8-l1 见过的 MNIST DataModule 骨架相同，但多了一个关键设计：**transform 不写死在类里，而是作为构造参数从外部注入**。这正是三份 notebook「只改一处」的支点——模型、优化器、循环全部不动，只换注入的 transform。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
构造 Cifar10DataModule(train_transform=..., test_transform=...)
        │
        ├─ prepare_data()   下载 CIFAR-10；若调用者没传 transform，
        │                   则兜底为 Resize + ToTensor（无增强、也无 Normalize）
        │
        ├─ setup()          train 数据集挂 train_transform（随机、每 epoch 不同）
        │                   test  数据集挂 test_transform（确定性）
        │                   再用 random_split 把 train 切成 45000 训练 + 5000 验证
        │
        └─ train/val/test_dataloader()   三个 DataLoader：训练集 shuffle+drop_last，
                                         验证/测试集不 shuffle
```

训练侧则完全复用 u8-l1 的范式：`LightningModel` 包住 `torchvision.models.resnet18`，`Trainer.fit` 一行启动。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看双 transform 接口的定义。`Cifar10DataModule.__init__` 接收外部注入的两套 transform 并原样保存：

- [helper_utilities.py:L63-L74](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/helper_utilities.py#L63-L74) —— 构造参数 `train_transform=None, test_transform=None`：训练与评估两套 transform 从外部注入，默认 `None` 交给后续兜底逻辑。

兜底逻辑在 `prepare_data` 里：下载 CIFAR-10 后，若没传 transform，则给训练/评估各配一份 `Resize + ToTensor`：

- [helper_utilities.py:L76-L94](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/helper_utilities.py#L76-L94) —— 下载 CIFAR-10；`train_transform is None` 时兜底为 `transforms.Compose([Resize(height_width), ToTensor()])`。注意这套兜底 transform **没有任何增强，也没有 Normalize**——基线 notebook 走的正是这条路径。

`setup` 把两套 transform 分别挂到数据集上：

- [helper_utilities.py:L96-L111](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/helper_utilities.py#L96-L111) —— 训练集（`train=True`）挂 `self.train_transform`，测试集（`train=False`）挂 `self.test_transform`；随后 `random_split(train, lengths=[45000, 5000])` 切出验证集。

**⚠️ 批判性读码点 1：验证集也被增强了。** 仔细读上面这段：`random_split` 切出的 `self.valid` 是「挂着 `train_transform` 的那个数据集」的子集，与 `self.train` 共享同一个 dataset 对象。也就是说，传了 AutoAugment 时，**验证集的每张图在每个 epoch 也会被随机增强一次**。这不同于 u4-l1 精读过的 `helper_data.py` 方案——那边用索引区间 + sampler 精确切分，让验证子集挂确定性的 `test_transforms`。后果是：本讲的 `val_acc` 是「模型在增强样本上的准确率」，口径偏向训练分布；不过由于验证集样本量大（5000 张）、增强是随机的，它仍能用于横向比较三种配置。读源码时认准变量来源，才能解释指标的确切含义。

三个 DataLoader 的构造在：

- [helper_utilities.py:L113-L141](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch-lightning_ipynb/data-augmentation/autoaugment/helper_utilities.py#L113-L141) —— 训练 loader `shuffle=True, drop_last=True`，验证/测试 loader 不打乱。与 u4-l1 讲过的批数公式、drop_last 语义一致。

训练侧的 `LightningModel`（SGD + 交叉熵 + torchmetrics 指标）在：

### 4.2 AutoAugment：搜索出来的增强策略

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

AutoAugment（Cubuk et al., 2019, [arXiv:1805.09501](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.09501)）把「设计增强规则」本身当成一个搜索问题：在代理任务上用强化学习为每个数据集搜出一套策略，策略由 25 个**子策略（sub-policy）**组成，每个子策略是两个有序操作 \((OP_1, P_1, M_1) \to (OP_2, P_2, M_2)\)，其中 \(P\) 是应用概率、\(M\) 是幅度（如旋转多少度、剪切多大）。训练时：

```text
取一张图 x
    │
    ├─ 从 25 个子策略中均匀随机抽 1 个（概率 1/25）
    ├─ 以概率 P1 执行操作1（强度 M1），否则跳过
    └─ 以概率 P2 执行操作2（强度 M2），否则跳过
```

CIFAR-10 策略用到的算子包括剪切、平移、旋转、色调/对比度/锐度调整、Posterize、Solarize、AutoContrast、Equalize 等。对普通使用者来说，这些搜索结果已内置在 torchvision 中——`transforms.autoaugment.AutoAugmentPolicy.CIFAR10` 一个枚举值就是整套 25 子策略。

它与手工增强（`RandomCrop` + `RandomHorizontalFlip`）的本质区别：手工增强靠人的直觉挑选两三种固定扰动；AutoAugment 靠数据搜出一大张「操作×概率×幅度」的组合表，扰动空间丰富得多。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

接入方式只是 u4-l3 Compose 流水线的一次「插拔」：

```text
transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize(32),                                  # 确定性：先统一尺寸
    transforms.AutoAugment(AutoAugmentPolicy.CIFAR10),      # 随机增强：PIL 域
    transforms.ToTensor(),                                  # PIL → Tensor，值域 [0,1]
])
        │
        └─ 注入 Cifar10DataModule(train_transform=...)
                │
                └─ 其余一切（模型/优化器/Trainer/seed）与基线相同
```

注意增强操作的位置：**在 `Resize` 之后、`ToTensor` 之前**——AutoAugment 的算子工作在 PIL 图像域，遵守 u4-l3 讲过的固定顺序「PIL 域变换 → ToTensor → （可选 Normalize）」。

增强对训练动态的影响：训练损失下降变慢（同一张图每个 epoch 长得都不一样，模型更难死记），因此需要**多得多的 epoch** 才能兑现收益——这正是 notebook 把 `max_epochs` 从 40 提到 500 的原因。

### 4.3 TrivialAugmentWide：免调参增强与三组对照

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

TrivialAugmentWide（Müller & Hutter, 2021, [arXiv:2103.10158](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10158)）是对 AutoAugment 复杂性的反思：既然搜索那么贵，干脆**不搜索**。规则简单到一段话讲完——

```text
取一张图 x
    ├─ 从算子池 {Rotate, ShearX, ShearY, TranslateX, TranslateY, Color, Contrast,
    │            Brightness, Sharpness, Posterize, Solarize, AutoContrast, Equalize, Identity}
    │            中均匀随机抽 1 个
    ├─ 从 [0, num_magnitude_bins] 均匀随机抽一个强度（默认 31 档，"Wide" 即指强度范围宽）
    └─ 无条件应用（没有 AutoAugment 那样的应用概率 P）
```

没有任何在目标任务上搜出来的参数，跨数据集零适配。论文结论是它以近乎零的成本追平或超过搜索类方法——「简单基线的胜利」。

对使用者的意义：AutoAugment 需要为数据集挑选对应 policy（`AutoAugmentPolicy.CIFAR10`/`IMAGENET`/`SVHN`），换数据集要动脑；TrivialAugmentWide 换数据集什么都不用改。本讲最后一组对照会检验：在这套仓库配置下，免调参的 TrivialAugment 是否真的不输 AutoAugment。

**练习 3**：假设你要把本讲增强迁移到自己的 10 类工业缺陷检测数据集（每类仅几百张图），先试哪种？要注意什么？

**答案**：先试 TrivialAugmentWide（零配置、对中小数据集通常稳健），但要审查算子是否破坏任务语义——例如缺陷颜色本身就是判别特征时，`Color`/`Solarize` 等颜色扰动可能抹掉类别差异；旋转若破坏方向语义（如文字、裂纹走向）也应排除。增强注入的是「标签不变的先验」，先验错了就帮倒忙。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
